source.title: Controlling Covariate Shift using Equilibrium Normalization of Weights

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The title in the supplied text differs from the catalog title: the text says “Balanced Normalization of Weights.”
record.tranche_reason: Compares a weight-space normalization method with BatchNorm and reports its training convergence on benchmark networks, bearing on V6's claim about normalization and training speed.
record.gate_note: The paper reports faster convergence for BalNorm than BatchNorm, but does not report training classification error. Test-accuracy and test-loss results do not establish the training-error outcome in the claim. Values from plots are not transcribed as training metrics.
record.test_reason: The study compares its proposed BalNorm method with BatchNorm and GroupNorm. It has no matched unnormalized baseline and does not test Fixup, so these comparisons do not establish or contradict V6's claimed benefit of adding BatchNorm. Its own results do not test V1–V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: BalNorm shows faster convergence than BatchNorm in the reported CIFAR comparisons but greater overfitting with the initial recipe. Additional regularization improves CIFAR generalization, while preliminary ImageNet experiments retain a generalization gap that manifold mixup did not resolve.
record.recipe_differences: Uses weight-space Balanced Normalization and compares it with batch normalization; the claim's normalization statement is related, but the paper does not test training classification error. It also reports GroupNorm comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: BalNorm shows overfitting on the initial CIFAR-10 recipe; using a quarter batch for statistics or manifold mixup changes generalization. On ImageNet, the reported generalization gap remains despite manifold mixup.

fits_no_version.finding: BalNorm converges faster than BatchNorm in the reported CIFAR experiments; quarter-batch statistics or manifold mixup improve its generalization. At 30 epochs, median test accuracy is 94.050% versus 93.319%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Balanced weight normalization can improve convergence relative to BatchNorm in the tested CIFAR recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: BalNorm and BatchNorm have similar final test accuracy on CIFAR-100 and SVHN, while ImageNet accuracy is lower for BalNorm: 74.88% versus 76.53%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization performance of BalNorm relative to BatchNorm depends on the dataset and recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that WeightNorm did not reliably converge on very deep architectures such as ResNet-152 despite substantial effort.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: WeightNorm can encounter convergence difficulties in very deep residual networks under the attempted recipes.

record.problems: The reported benchmark outcomes are primarily test accuracy and test loss, not training classification error. The ImageNet experiment is described as preliminary and has three runs. The text provides plots rather than numeric convergence measures for several comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant numeric training-error results are reported. Figure-only test-loss curves and test-accuracy values were not extracted as separate rows when they duplicated the separately reported endpoint accuracy or did not provide a numeric training metric.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, including random labels and model-size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut controls, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Comparative initialization effects on propagation, learning speed, and trainable depth; the sign-resampling recommendation has no measured initialization comparison.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, loss recovery, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Adding BatchNorm versus leaving the same network unnormalized, including accuracy gained over training and higher learning-rate tolerance; comparable speed and stability with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The extraction incorrectly treats training classification error as necessary for V6: accuracy gained faster over training can bear on that version. Here the decisive problem is the missing unnormalized comparison, not simply the use of test metrics. Neither BalNorm nor GroupNorm is the specified Fixup alternative.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error from random initialization, including with corrupted or random labels and the stated size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects on training error with and without identity shortcuts, and the special initialization or normalization-free residual comparisons.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Training above the stability limit, curvature or sharpness changes, recovery, and divergence.

Reports faster convergence for BalNorm than BatchNorm, but does not quantify accuracy gained over training on the listed CIFAR networks. Does not test the full set of versions' normalization and architecture settings, or Fixup residual networks.

rows.measure: Convergence speed; no numeric training-error result stated.
rows.baseline: BalNorm converged significantly faster; numeric baseline not stated.
rows.value: BatchNorm convergence was significantly slower than BalNorm.
rows.note: The paper says BalNorm converged significantly faster than BatchNorm, but does not quantify training error or report zero training classification error.
rows.check: BalNorm versus BatchNorm convergence is the proposed method's performance comparison, not BatchNorm versus an unnormalized network. Slower convergence than BalNorm does not make V6 partial.
